# General remarks

:::medium
This is an [**examination-only term.**]{.fragment .fade-in}
[There are no lectures in the winter term 2026/2027.]{.fragment .fade-in}
[You prepare on your own and sit an oral examination.]{.fragment .fade-in}
:::

:::notes
The course is taught in the summer term. The winter term offers the examination only, so there are no classes, no weekly sessions, and no in-class exercises.

The lecture notes from the summer term 2026 are the study material and the reference for everything you will be asked in the examination. You are expected to work through them independently:

- [Introduction](../../26ST/introduction/slides.html): what emerging technologies are, the process of emergence, and the five attributes that characterize them
- [Multimodality and Immersion](../../26ST/immersion/slides.html) (`H1`)
- [Intelligence and Affection](../../26ST/intelligence/slides.html) (`H2`)
- [Interconnectedness and Distributivity](../../26ST/interconnectedness/slides.html) (`H3`)
- [Mobility and Ubiquity](../../26ST/ubiquity/slides.html) (`H4`)

Alongside the notes, @suh2018state and @dellermann2019hybrid are the two core readings; both are referenced throughout the units.
:::

# Learning objectives

During this course, you should advance your skills in the following areas:

:::incremental
- understanding of the **key characteristics of emerging technologies** in general, the process and phases of technology emergence, as well as specific characteristics of emerging information technologies/digital technologies,
- knowledge of **fields of application** of current merging digital technologies, their impact on (information) systems used by individuals, organizations, and society, as well as media
- understanding of **potentials and risks** for individuals, economies and societies,
- communication of conclusions and the underlying knowledge,
- and social and ethical responsibilities in uncertain and ambiguous contexts.
:::

# Effort

::: {.html-hidden .large}
[5 ECTS]{.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}\
[≈ 150 h workload]{.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}\
[≈ 50 h self-study of the lecture notes]{.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}\
[+ 100 h technology analysis and exam preparation]{.fragment .fade-in-then-semi-out}
:::

:::notes
You will gain 5 ECTS for this course. This equals approx. __150 hours workload__, of which you need most to pass the course. Because there are no classes, the whole workload is self-directed:

- Working through the lecture notes of the summer term 2026 (approx. 50 hours)
- Researching your assigned technology and preparing the slides (approx. 80 hours)
- Consolidating the theory for the Q&A (approx. 20 hours)
:::

:::fragment
Reserve enough time to study the lecture notes **and** prepare your presentation (see @tbl-schedule for the dates).
:::

# Examination

:::medium
Graded will be
[your **introduction to an assigned emerging digital technology**]{.fragment .fade-in}
[in a short presentation of approx. 8 minutes,]{.fragment .fade-in}
[and **your ability to answer theory-based questions**]{.fragment .fade-in}
[in a Q&A of approx. 8 minutes.]{.fragment .fade-in}
:::

:::notes
The examination has two parts. First you introduce your assigned technology so that the audience gains a solid understanding of it. Afterwards I ask you questions about the emergent nature of that technology and about the four hypotheses discussed in the lecture notes, which you answer in theory-based terms.

The Q&A carries the larger share of the grade. Details see [here](../assignment/index.qmd).
:::
